findings.reason: Confirmed (high). The standing data on p. 677 fixes Q_i of degree at most d_i before defining Poly(H), and Theorem 1.2 (p. 675) repeats deg Q_i ≤ d_i. Theorem 1.5 works 'in the assumptions of Theorem 1.2'. Theorem 1.9 (p. 680) does not restate the degree condition, but its R(x, H) divides by #Poly(H) as defined on p. 677. Item 9 says no degree condition is required, and item 11 inherits item 9's data, adding only coprimality. The witness is right. Take n = d_1 = 1, M = 2, n_0 = 0 and Q = t² + 1. Then Q(0) = 1 is prime to 2, but no linear P agrees with Q coefficientwise modulo 2, so Poly(H) is empty for every H. Item 11's density-one statement then has an empty denominator, which item 2's own test rejects. The fix, restoring deg Q_i ≤ d_i (or deg(Q_i mod M) ≤ d_i) in item 11 and in route 1's contract, is right.

Confirmed (medium). Proposition 3.8 (p. 694) assumes H^{δ₁} ≤ z ≤ H, and item l1-bound-truncated-von-mangoldt drops this range. The sum S_F(0) runs over all c ∈ Z with |c| ≤ (d+1)𝓜^d H (p. 691), so it includes c = 0. With Λ_z(r) = −Σ_{d ≤ z, d | r} μ(d) log d (p. 691), every d divides 0. So Λ_p(0) − Λ_{p−1}(0) = −μ(p) log p = log p at each prime p. For fixed H, |Λ_z(0)| is therefore unbounded in z, while the item's bound H(log H)²𝓜^d is fixed. The item's own note, z log z ≤ H log H, uses z ≤ H. The fix, restoring a z-range (1 ≤ z ≤ H suffices for the zero term, or the source range), is right, and Proposition 3.8 itself is not in error.
